summary: Hans T. Bakker (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink (~1972–1984). He held posts at the University of Groningen (~1989–2013) and served as a curator at the British Museum in 2014.

Hans Windisch (1881–1935) was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1926–1929), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1929–1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (1939–1999) worked in religious, Iranian and Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded as Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indologist who studied under Eduard Hermann and doctoral supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973).
Hansa Dhammahaso works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, he was attested as Director at the International Buddhist Studies College and director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Hanung Kim is a Tibetology and Sinology scholar. He earned a master's degree at Columbia University and completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal (1884–1939) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He pursued studies at the University of Delhi (~1901–1903) and later studied at SOAS University of London (~1927–1932).
Har Dutt Sharma (d. 1942) was an Indology scholar who served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and was attested at Hindu College, University of Delhi, in 1957.

Hara Prasad Sastri (1853–1931) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).
Harabhatta Sastri is an Indologist attested between 1918 and 1945 as holding posts, including as a Pandit, at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.
Harabhatha Shastri is an Indology scholar who served at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, where he is attested as Pandit in 1911 and 1916.

Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg (Promotion 1964), and FU Berlin (Habilitation). He held professorships at Berlin and Heidelberg (1980–1994) and served as director at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and DAI Istanbul.
Harald Hundius (1939–2019) was a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Singkha Wannasai. In 1983, he was a lecturer at Chiang Mai University.

Haraprasad Shastri (1853–1931) studied at Sanskrit College and Presidency College. An Indologist, Buddhist scholar, and historian, he served as Principal of Benares Sanskrit College, taught at Presidency, and headed the Department of Bengali and Sanskrit at Dhaka University.

Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948), and Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Ramakant Tripathi and completed doctoral studies under Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Scottish Church College and Calcutta University, he taught at Scottish Church College, Calcutta University, the University of Dhaka, and Banaras Hindu University.
Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi is an Indologist who studied under Karunapati Tripathi and served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Muni Jinavijaya and held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965), Gujarat University (1965–1975), and the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (~1975–1990).

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University. In ~1987, he was appointed to a chair at the University of British Columbia.
